text: {"side":"artifact","claims":[{"text":"The known-issue checklist flags deep_limit_suspect on 29 of 31 points, so most of the event's non-detections sit at plate limits that may not reach the depth needed to see the star reliably.","evidence_ids":["E-062","E-025","E-026","E-027"]},{"text":"The disappearance rests on non-detections, not detections: every point in the event's listing has offset_mag null and detection false, so the drop depends on limiting magnitudes rather than on measured brightness.","evidence_ids":["E-025","E-033","E-046","E-054"]},{"text":"The two points not tagged DEEP_LIMIT_SUSPECT (E-033 and E-046) have limiting offsets near 1.0 mag, so the only clean non-detections are shallow ones; the deep-limit tags on the rest suggest the drop may reflect plate depth rather than a real fading.","evidence_ids":["E-033","E-046","E-062"]},{"text":"The dnb series has a median zero-point offset of -1.489 mag from a single point, and the event's points are dominated by dnb plates from 1980 to 1989, so a series-level calibration offset could produce an apparent step at the seam between plate series.","evidence_ids":["E-016","E-026","E-054","E-055"]},{"text":"Block 3 omits one of the 31 trigger points by a strongest-half and even-sample rule, so the packet cannot confirm whether the dropped point would have changed the disappearance pattern; the missing point is a gap I cannot evaluate.","evidence_ids":["E-055","E-002"]}]}
